machine_boundary.windows_host: HP OMEN 16-ap0xxx — workstation 2, Windows 11 10.0.26200. Only the machine WSL2 runs on; no Windows browser was involved.
machine_boundary.note: EVERY result here was measured INSIDE the Linux guest. S-02 (Windows Firefox) is a SEPARATE CELL and its ACCEPT is not extended by this experiment.

browser.name: Mozilla Firefox
browser.source: Mozilla official linux64 tarball (download.mozilla.org, product=firefox-latest-ssl) — deliberately NOT the Ubuntu apt package, which on 26.04 is a snap transitional stub that does not work well under WSL2
browser.same_version_as_windows_cell: yes — Firefox 155.0.1 on both, which makes the Windows/Linux comparison a platform comparison rather than a version comparison

extension_loading.background: background.scripts — the Firefox MV3 EVENT PAGE

gpu_state.nvidia_smi_in_guest: WORKS — NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5050 Laptop GPU, 8151 MiB, driver 592.82
gpu_state.dev_dri: ABSENT — /dev/dri does not exist in this WSL2 guest
gpu_state.critical_note: nvidia-smi working is the CUDA COMPUTE path. The GRAPHICS stack in this guest is software-only. These are separate measurements and must not be conflated — see the experiment README.

preferences.dom.webgpu.enabled: variant 1 leaves it UNTOUCHED (release defaults) and that variant alone decides ACCEPT/REJECT. Variant 3 sets it to true and is recorded SEPARATELY, because the pre-registered criteria say a result requiring an about:config change on the release channel is CONDITIONAL, never ACCEPT.
preferences.extensions.originControls.grantByDefault: set to true in all variants. Affects only how the probe REPORTS (Firefox MV3 gates host_permissions), never what is measured.

data.payloads: synthetic Int32Array of i % 1024, verified against a CPU reference
data.profiles: fresh temporary profile per run, deleted afterwards
